implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosure is a mandatory stop-gate in Indian M&A: acquisition of 25%+ triggers open offer; careful timing and sequencing of disclosures is critical to avoid trading violations and to plan the tender structure.

framework.note: Mandatory disclosure of acquisition of shares or voting rights by an acquirer; triggers review of whether open offer obligation arises (25%+ threshold or control).
Definition of 'acquirer' and 'acquisition'; clarifies when disclosure is triggered (direct, indirect, deemed).
Exemptions to open offer: inter-se transfers among promoters, acquisition from open market up to 5%, etc.
Open offer obligation: acquisition of 25%+ or acquisition resulting in control requires mandatory offer to all shareholders at specified price.
Price discovery mechanism: minimum offer price determined by SEBI formula (6-month or 2-year VWAP, or negotiated price if PAC approval obtained).
SEBI's rule-making power; provides statutory foundation for SAST Regulations.
Directors' approval and board notice of material changes in shareholding or control; dovetails with SEBI disclosure.
Nominee shareholder rules and beneficial ownership disclosure; relevant if acquisition is routed through a DP or HUF.

headline: Chandrakant Vallabhaji Gogri triggers substantial acquisition disclosure in Aarti Industries
sum: Promoter/substantial shareholder Chandrakant Vallabhaji Gogri filed a Regulation 31(4) disclosure under SEBI's Takeover Code, signalling a material change in shareholding or triggering of open-offer obligations in the specialty chemicals manufacturer.
detail: Aarti Industries Limited, a listed specialty chemicals manufacturer, saw a substantial acquisition disclosure filed by Chandrakant Vallabhaji Gogri under Regulation 31(4) of SEBI (SAST) Regulations, 2011. The disclosure was submitted to NSE on or around 18 June 2026. The exact consideration, final shareholding percentage, and whether an open offer is mandatory remain to be disclosed in subsequent filings (Form C, PAC order if applicable). This is the mandatory pre-offer notice stage.
